problems.title: Successive fuel reductions
problems.question: A car uses 25% of its fuel, then 20% of what remains. It has 27 litres left. Find the initial amount.
problems.idea: Apply each percentage to the correct remaining amount.
steps: The remaining fraction is 0.75·0.8=0.6.
If the initial amount is F, then 0.6F=27, so F=45.

problems.title: Divisibility by a linear factor
problems.question: Find p so that 3x³+16x²+9x+p is divisible by x+3.
problems.idea: A root of the divisor must be a root of the polynomial.
formulas: Remainder theorem: divisibility by x-r requires P(r)=0.
steps: Set this to zero.

problems.title: Count intersections with concurrency
problems.question: How many distinct intersection points can four distinct pairwise nonparallel lines in a plane have?
problems.idea: Separate the possible numbers of concurrent lines.
formulas: Four lines have C(4,2)=6 intersecting pairs.
steps: If all four pass through one point, there is 1 intersection.
If exactly three are concurrent, their three pair-intersections merge into one and the fourth line meets them at three further points: 4 total.
If no three are concurrent, all 6 pair-intersections are distinct. Two different triple-concurrency points would force a common pair of lines to meet twice.

problems.title: An angle equals a difference of exterior angles
problems.question: One triangle interior angle equals the difference of the two nonadjacent exterior angles. Classify the triangle.
problems.idea: Exterior angles are supplements of the corresponding interior angles.
steps: The condition is A=|(180°-B)-(180°-C)|=|C-B|.
If C≥B, then C=A+B, so 2C=180° and C=90°.
If B≥C, the same argument gives B=90°.

problems.title: An equal secant segment triples a central angle
problems.question: AB is a diameter of a circle centred at O. C is beyond B on its line; a secant through C meets the circle at distinct E,D, with CE=OA. Find ∠AOD/∠BOE.
problems.idea: Normalize the radius and use the equal-length condition, retaining either order of E,D.
formulas: Power of C: CE·CD=CO²-R²; cos3θ=4cos³θ-3cosθ; sin3θ=(4cos²θ-1)sinθ.
steps: Put O=(0,0),B=(R,0),A=(-R,0), and let θ=∠BOE. Since OE=CE=R, the isosceles triangle gives C=(2Rcosθ,0), E=(Rcosθ,Rsinθ).
The power equation gives CD=R(4cos²θ-1). Moving this distance along the secant from C gives D=(-Rcos3θ,Rsin3θ).
Because C is outside the circle, 0<θ<60° for a genuine secant. The polar angle of D is 180°-3θ, so ∠AOD=3θ.
The same coordinates work whether E is the nearer or farther secant intersection.

problems.title: A diagonal splits the trapezoid midline
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid’s diagonal splits its midline into lengths 2 and 5 cm. Its leg is 6 cm. Find its angles.
problems.idea: The two midline pieces are half the two bases.
steps: The bases are 4 and 10, so each leg’s horizontal projection is (10-4)/2=3.
Thus cosα=3/6=1/2, giving the acute base angle 60°.
The adjacent angle is its supplement, 120°.

problems.title: A right angle between two tangent-circle chords
problems.question: Two circles touch externally at A. A common external tangent touches them at B,C. Find ∠BAC.
problems.idea: Use equal tangent lengths from the tangent’s intersection with the common tangent at A.
formulas: Tangent segments from one exterior point to the same circle are equal.
steps: Let T be where BC meets the common tangent at A. Then TA=TB and TA=TC.
Thus T is the midpoint of BC and TA=TB=TC. A lies on the circle with centre T and diameter BC.
An angle subtending a diameter is right.

problems.title: Cancel a difference of cubes
problems.question: Simplify $\dfrac{\sqrt y}{27-y\sqrt y}(1+3/\sqrt y+9/y)$.
problems.idea: Set t=√y.
steps: The domain is y>0 and y≠9. The expression becomes t/(27-t³)·(t²+3t+9)/t².
Cancel the common quadratic factor to get 1/[t(3-t)].
Replace t by √y.

problems.title: A parameter giving a positive linear root
problems.question: For which t does 3(2-x)=4(t-2x) have a positive root?
problems.idea: Solve for x first.
steps: Since the denominator 5 is positive, x>0 iff 4t-6>0.
Thus t>3/2.
problems.note: A single choice t=2 is an example, and (1.5,5) is a subset of valid values, but the full parameter set is (1.5,∞).

problems.title: Rationalize three denominators
problems.question: Evaluate $2/(\sqrt3-1)+3/(\sqrt3-2)+15/(3-\sqrt3)$.
problems.idea: Multiply each fraction by its conjugate.
steps: The three terms become √3+1, -3√3-6, and (15/6)(3+√3).
Combine constants: 1-6+15/2=5/2. Combine √3 coefficients: 1-3+5/2=1/2.

problems.title: Largest ratio with positive bounds
problems.question: Find the largest a/b if 1≤a≤4 and 2≤b≤6.
problems.idea: Increase the numerator and decrease the positive denominator.
formulas: For positive b, a/b increases with a and decreases with b when a>0.
steps: Choose a=4 and b=2.
The value 4/2=2 is attainable and bounds every allowed ratio.

problems.title: An integer just above a radical
problems.question: Find the smallest integer greater than √10+√40.
problems.idea: Combine the radicals and bound the result.
steps: The sum is 3√10=√90.
It lies strictly between 9 and 10, so the next integer is 10.

problems.title: Reduce the input by the period
problems.question: The plotted function has period 6. Find f(26).
problems.idea: Use an equivalent input visible in the plot.
steps: The marked graph vertex at x=2 has y=1.

problems.title: Central angles from isosceles radius triangles
problems.question: On the shown circle, ∠BAO=20° and ∠BCO=30°. Find the marked smaller ∠AOC.
problems.idea: Each pair of radii forms an isosceles triangle.
formulas: An isosceles triangle with base angle β has apex angle 180°-2β; angles around a point total 360°.
steps: The diagram places these two angles around the other side of O, leaving ∠AOC=360°-140°-120°=100°.

problems.title: Compose increasing and decreasing functions
problems.question: f increases on ℝ and g decreases on ℝ. How does f(g(x)) vary?
problems.idea: Follow the order through both functions.
formulas: An increasing function preserves an inequality; a decreasing function reverses it.
steps: For x₁<x₂, g(x₁)>g(x₂).
Applying increasing f gives f(g(x₁))>f(g(x₂)).

problems.title: A common remainder modulo 3 and 5
problems.question: Find the greatest two-digit integer leaving remainder 2 on division by both 3 and 5.
problems.idea: Subtract the common remainder.
formulas: If n-2 is divisible by 3 and 5, it is divisible by lcm(3,5)=15.
steps: The candidates are n=15k+2.
The largest below 100 is 15·6+2=92; the next is 107.

problems.title: Vertical angles transfer a triangle angle
problems.question: In the diagram AC and DE cross at B, ∠BAE=35°, ∠AEB=90°, and DB=DC. Find ∠BDC.
problems.idea: Find ∠ABE, then use vertical angles and an isosceles triangle.
formulas: Triangle angles sum to 180°; vertical angles are equal.
steps: ∠ABE=180°-35°-90°=55°. Its vertical angle ∠DBC is 55°.
DB=DC makes the base angles at B,C both 55°.

problems.title: Equal tangent lengths between two touching circles
problems.question: The pictured external tangents touch two externally tangent circles at A,B and C,D. The common tangent at their touching point meets them at E,F. Find EF if CD=7.5.
problems.idea: Use the tangent lengths on both sides of the touching point.
formulas: Two external common tangent segments between the circles have equal length; tangent segments from the same exterior point are equal.
steps: Let T be the circle touching point. EA=EB=ET, so AB=2ET. Similarly FC=FD=FT, so CD=2FT.
The two common external tangent lengths satisfy AB=CD=7.5. Thus ET=FT=3.75.
T lies between E,F in the diagram, so EF=ET+FT=7.5.

problems.title: Speed is the slope of a distance graph
problems.question: From the plotted distance-time graph, identify when the tourist moves at 2 km/h.
problems.idea: Read a segment’s rise divided by its duration.
steps: From t=0.5 to 1.5 hours, distance rises from 4 to 6 km.
The speed is (6-4)/(1.5-0.5)=2 km/h.
The other listed segments have different slopes; a flat segment represents rest.

problems.title: Rewrite all powers in one base
problems.question: Simplify $3^{-5+2n}/9^{n-3}$.
problems.idea: Use 9=3².
steps: The denominator is 3^(2n-6).
Subtract exponents: -5+2n-(2n-6)=1.

problems.title: A parallel line through a point
problems.question: Find the line parallel to y=2x+1 through (2,3).
problems.idea: Parallel nonvertical lines have the same slope.
steps: Use slope m=2.

problems.title: The angle between two internal bisectors
problems.question: In triangle ABC, B=40° and the A,C bisectors meet at D. Find ∠ADC.
problems.idea: The other two angles of triangle ADC are halves of A,C.
steps: A+C=140°, so their half-angle sum is 70°.
The remaining angle at D is 180°-70°=110°.

problems.title: The square root restricts a product equation
problems.question: Solve $\sqrt x(x^3+8)=0$ over the reals.
problems.idea: Check the square-root domain before using zero factors.
formulas: √x exists for x≥0; a product is zero iff a factor is zero.
steps: The first factor is zero at x=0, which works.
The second factor is zero at x=-2, but this is outside the real domain.

problems.title: Use a cyclic angle and the external triangle
problems.question: In the shown cyclic quadrilateral ABCE, ∠ABC=90°, ∠BCE=125°. D is the exterior intersection of AE and BC. Find ∠ADC.
problems.idea: Opposite cyclic angles are supplementary.
steps: ∠BAE=55°. Since D lies on the ray AE, ∠BAD=55°.
Also ∠ABD=∠ABC=90° because B,C,D are collinear as shown.
Thus ∠ADB=180°-90°-55°=35°, equal to ∠ADC.

problems.title: Strict triangle inequalities
problems.question: A triangle has two sides 6 and 8 cm. Which of 14,15,1,11 can be its third side?
problems.idea: The third side must be strictly between the difference and sum.
steps: Here 2<c<14.
Only 11 satisfies both strict bounds; 14 would give a degenerate triangle.

problems.title: A weighted average of ages
problems.question: Thirty women average 30 years and twenty men average 40 years. Find the average for all fifty teachers.
problems.idea: Average total age using the group sizes as weights.
steps: The total age is 30·30+20·40=1700.
Divide by 50 to get 34.

problems.title: The vertex gives the maximum
problems.question: Where does y=-x²+4x+11 attain its maximum on [0,10]?
problems.idea: Complete the square.
steps: The squared term is smallest at x=2, inside the interval.
The maximum value is 15, attained there.

problems.title: The farthest two allowed endpoints
problems.question: Find the largest |a-b| for 1≤a≤3 and 4≤b≤6.
problems.idea: Here b is always greater than a.
steps: Maximize b-a by choosing b=6,a=1.
This gives 5, attainable within the bounds.

problems.title: Parallel lines preserve the reference direction
problems.question: In the shown diagram, AB makes 15° with a horizontal line and AC makes 65° with a parallel horizontal line. Find ∠BAC.
problems.idea: Transfer both directions to a parallel through A.
formulas: Corresponding angles formed by parallel lines are equal.
steps: The rays AB,AC point to the same side of the reference parallel through A.
Their inclinations differ by 65°-15°=50°.

problems.title: Perimeter of a triangle bounded by tangents
problems.question: In the diagram AB=8 cm is a circle tangent from A. A third tangent at K cuts the two rays at E,F before B,C. Find the perimeter of AEF.
problems.idea: Match tangent segments from E and F.
steps: The perimeter is AE+AF+EF=AE+AF+EK+KF.
Replace EK by EB and KF by FC.
Then the sum is (AE+EB)+(AF+FC)=AB+AC=8+8=16.

problems.title: A linear equation true for every x
problems.question: Find a,b so that (a+b)x-2b=bx+3 has infinitely many solutions.
problems.idea: The simplified coefficient and constant must both match.
formulas: An identity Ax=B for all x requires A=0 and B=0.
steps: Subtract bx to get ax=2b+3.
Thus a=0 and 2b+3=0.

problems.title: A line through the origin and an intersection
problems.question: Find the line through (0,0) and the intersection of 4x+5y=14, -5x+2y=18.
problems.idea: Solve the intersection, then use its direction.
formulas: A line through the origin has equation ux+vy=0.
steps: Elimination gives x=-62/33,y=142/33.
Their ratio gives y/x=-71/31.
Thus 71x+31y=0.

problems.title: An inconsistent pair of parallel equations
problems.question: For which m does mx+5y=3, 2x+y=4 have no solution?
problems.idea: Make the left sides proportional but not the constants.
formulas: A singular two-equation system has determinant m-10=0.
steps: The only candidate is m=10.
The second equation multiplied by 5 is 10x+5y=20, contradicting 10x+5y=3.
For every m≠10 the determinant is nonzero, giving one solution.

problems.title: Combine monthly percentages with tonnages
problems.question: In January firm I imports 55% and firm II 45%. In February they import 600 and 1200 tonnes. Over both months their shares are 40%,60%. Find each two-month total.
problems.idea: Let J be January’s total.
steps: Solve 0.15J=120 to get J=800.
The combined 2600 tonnes split 1040:1560=40:60.
problems.answer: Firm I: 1040 tonnes; firm II: 1560 tonnes.

problems.title: A repeated product root gives two pairs
problems.question: Solve $xy+4/(xy)=4$, $2x-y=4$.
problems.idea: First determine the product xy.
steps: Thus xy=2 and y=2x-4.
Substitute: 2x²-4x=2, giving x=1±√2.
Then y=-2±2√2 with matching signs; both pairs have product 2.

problems.title: The director changes the average
problems.question: The director is 22 years older than the meeting average including himself, and 24 years older than the average excluding himself. How many others attend?
problems.idea: Express both averages using the same director age.
steps: Let the director age be D and the number of others n. Their mean is D-24.
The combined mean is [n(D-24)+D]/(n+1)=D-24n/(n+1).
It also equals D-22, so 24n=22(n+1), giving n=11.

problems.title: Two investments with different profits
problems.question: Two share packages cost 31250 lari total and sell for 40000. Their respective profits are 40% and 20%. Find each initial cost.
problems.idea: Use selling-price multipliers rather than adding percentages.
steps: Subtract 1.2 times the first equation from the second: 0.2x=2500.
Thus x=12500 and y=18750.
Their selling values 17500 and 22500 total 40000.

problems.title: Two quadratics share their two roots
problems.question: The plotted quadratics y=ax²+x+c and y=x²+px+q meet only at their x-axis crossings. The downward parabola has y-intercept -1; the upward one has 5. Find a,c,p,q.
problems.idea: Two quadratics with the same two roots are scalar multiples.
steps: The graph gives c=-1 and q=5.
Compare constants: -1=5a, so a=-1/5.
Compare x coefficients: 1=ap, so p=-5.

problems.title: Construct four parameter pairs with the same interval
problems.question: Give four pairs (a,b) so that ax>b+1, bx<a+10 has solution set (-∞,-2).
problems.idea: Make the first inequality exactly x<-2 and the second less restrictive.
steps: Take (a,b)=(-1,1),(-2,3),(-3,5),(-4,7). Each first inequality is x<-2.
Their second inequalities respectively give x<9,x<8/3,x<7/5,x<6/7, all weaker than x<-2.
Therefore each intersection is exactly the required open interval.

problems.title: Integer intercepts become divisor pairs
problems.question: Find all lines through (5,13) whose x- and y-intercepts have nonnegative integer coordinates.
problems.idea: For distinct intercepts, use intercept form and factor a product.
steps: With positive intercepts u,v, the point forces u>5,v>13. The positive ordered factor pairs of 65 are (1,65),(5,13),(13,5),(65,1).
If the two intercepts may coincide at the origin, y=13x/5 also qualifies: both axis intersections are (0,0). It is the only such extra line.
problems.answer: Four lines with distinct intercepts: 13x+y=78; 13x+5y=130; x+y=18; x+5y=70. Also 13x-5y=0 if coincident zero intercepts are allowed.
problems.note: The word “nonnegative” allows zero. Excluding the origin case requires the additional convention that the two intercept points are distinct.
